before.description_1: The biggest obstacle for Palmeroshop involved presenting the offer in a way that would be quickly understandable. This meant that the page needed to make clear what the offer included, who it served, and why contact should be initiated, without using generic phrases that could apply equally well to another site.
before.description_2: I simplified the beauty story by adding an impactful introduction, defining services in clear sections, and putting practical information close to action points. The WordPress layout enables fast browsing, both on desktop and mobile devices, making it easy for visitors to comprehend the offer and choose to connect with Palmeroshop. This made a lot of sense.

after.description_1: Palmero Shop is an ecommerce site for massage guns and recovery accessories. Product education, supporting articles, FAQs, delivery and return information all need to work together so customers understand the products before they decide to buy.
after.description_2: I structured the WooCommerce experience around product-led browsing, clear product explanations and a direct shopping route. Educational content supports the purchase decision without interrupting it, while store policies and FAQs remain easy to reach before checkout.

before.description_1: The Energy page for Solar Daktechnique entailed the removal of any sort of reservations before proceeding to inquire about anything. This visitor was likely comparing other firms, and therefore it was necessary to clarify what the firm had to offer and what steps followed thereafter. The use of general language would have caused confusion.
before.description_2: I have made the way simpler to move through shorter headings, more specific descriptions for projects, and also WordPress post information that is quite easy to maintain in the future. It not only enhances the presentation of Solar Daktechnique but also ensures that no visitor finds any difficulty browsing through the portfolio or contacting the company.

after.description_1: Solar Daktechnique presents solar panels, charging solutions and related electrical work through a technical energy-services website. Visitors needed to understand the available solutions and the company’s practical role before requesting a quotation or making contact.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content around the main energy-service choices, supporting technical information and clear quotation routes. The first layer stays easy to scan, while deeper detail remains available for visitors who want to compare solutions before enquiring.

before.description_1: Neutralhome needed content that was easier on the eyes and would make it easy to compare the various services available to them. The page needed to describe the interior design work done, without making the content hard to read, and at the same time provide enough information so as to convince someone to contact the company.
before.description_2: I structured the page around what visitors need to understand first: the offer, the value, and the next step. Clearer paragraphs, concise wording, and focused WordPress delivery make the interior project easier to assess and more convincing for potential inquiries.

after.description_1: Netural Home combines sanitary products, floors, tiles and renovation projects with showroom advice. The website needed to work as an inspiration layer first, then help visitors translate what they see into a practical appointment or quotation.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around product and renovation categories, project inspiration and tailored showroom advice. Visitors can browse ideas, understand the available interior options and move naturally toward an appointment or quote without losing the visual focus.

before.description_1: Oxford Academy's content was supposed to be made more precise in order to avoid having visitors guessing about the offerings of the education project. What was needed was well-structured, clear content with appropriate wording that provided adequate information for building trust but did not make initial contact complicated.
before.description_2: I created a clearer page structure with simple language, balanced sections, and contact moments placed where visitors are ready to act. The result is an education website that is easier to follow and more convincing for prospective students or parents.

after.description_1: Oxford Academy brings tutoring, homework guidance, exam preparation, remedial support and school services together across its education offering. The website needed to help parents and students understand those options, locations and approach before choosing a trial lesson or signup route.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around the main education services, the academy’s step-by-step approach, teacher and review proof and clear registration actions. The structure keeps the different forms of support distinct while making the next step easy to find.

before.description_1: The website was in need for Marcosmontage due to certain issues. First of all, there should have been enough information provided about the offer regarding the exhibition. Secondly, there should have been enough detail provided about the contact information of the owner of the gallery and the place itself.
before.description_2: I worked on the page by eliminating any form of repetition and reorganizing the structure of the content in a more concise way. This WordPress site is able to present the proposal in its practical context and with a steady pace that makes it easy for visitors to find their motivation.

after.description_1: Marcos Montage is an installation-services website, not an exhibition or gallery project. The website needed to explain the practical technical work clearly and give prospective customers a direct route from the relevant service to quotation or contact.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress presentation around concise service information and visible enquiry actions. The corrected portfolio copy removes the unrelated gallery references and describes the actual installation-focused customer journey across desktop and mobile.

before.description_1: Homeplaza needed stronger page copy because important information about the interior offer was not clear enough at the start. Visitors needed a more engaging introduction, a better structure and a simple explanation of the service before deciding to contact the company.
before.description_2: I improved the clarity of the site with a stronger structure and more natural English. The service information is easier to scan, easier to compare and more consistent across the WordPress presentation, helping visitors understand the offer before taking action.

after.description_1: Home Plaza covers kitchens, bathrooms, floors, wall finishes, steel doors, custom cabinetry, stair renovation and complete home renovation. The website needed to make that broad interior offer browsable while connecting inspiration and showroom information to a practical project process.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the main renovation categories, project steps and showroom proof. Visitors can move from exploring a specific part of the home to arranging an appointment or quotation, while the overall presentation still feels like one complete renovation proposition.

before.description_1: In the case of Brightlyn, the major difficulty was in ensuring that the offer on cybersecurity was clear enough for the potential customers in just a few seconds. The web page needed to be able to show what the offer entailed, which group would benefit from it, and why it makes sense to get in touch.
before.description_2: The process involved converting the story on cyber security into a simplified experience that had a stronger introduction and service blocks that were easier to understand, with relevant information close to where action needed to be taken. This was made possible because of the ease of navigating the website on mobile and desktops.

after.description_1: Brightlyn is a cybersecurity and regulatory consultancy whose services cover risk, resilience, DORA, NIS2 and assurance. The website needed to translate complex advisory subjects into clear service routes while showing the sectors and end-to-end approach behind the work.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content around the main cybersecurity and compliance needs, sector context and direct consultation options. The structure makes technical regulation easier to scan without oversimplifying the expertise, helping business visitors identify the relevant advisory route.

before.description_1: YCO IT needed an offer that visitors could understand within a few seconds. The page had to explain the services, who they are for, and why someone should get in touch, without relying on broad phrases that could apply to almost any company.
before.description_2: I simplified the compliance story into a more linear page structure, with a stronger introduction, clearer service blocks, and specific information at the right action points. The website is easier to scan on desktop and mobile, helping visitors understand the offer and decide whether to contact YCO IT.

after.description_1: YCO IT focuses on risk management and compliance, including subjects such as ISAE, ISO 27001 and 27701, control concepts and security or compliance assessments. The website needed to make those specialist services understandable to organisations evaluating governance and assurance support.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the main compliance and risk topics, practical assessment routes and clear contact points. Technical standards remain visible as proof of scope, while the page hierarchy helps visitors identify which service matches their organisation’s need.
